title: Tom Lee：AI 回檔傷害科技股，但「藍色海嘯」有利科技／AI
subtitle: TOM LEE: AI downturn is hurting Technology. We believe a 'blue tsunami' is helpful to Tech/AI stocks

credit.video_title: TOM LEE: AI downturn is hurting Technology. We believe a 'blue tsunami' is helpful to Tech/AI stocks

sentences.en: Hi there, this is Tom Lee.
I'm the chief investment officer of Fundstrat Capital and the lead portfolio manager for Fundstrat Capital's family of ETFs called Granny Shots.
This is our update for the week of November 2nd.
First, let me start with some particulars.
As of October 30th, the large cap Granny or ticker GRNY had assets of 4.23 billion.
The junior Granny, ticker GRNJ, had assets of 445 million.
And Granny I, ticker GRNI, had total assets of 57 million.
Over the past week, Granny Shots, fell 1.2% compared to a 0.6% decline in the S&P 500, which is 65 basis points of relative underperformance.
GRNJ rose 0.89% compared to a 1% rise for the Russell 2500 or 30 basis points of underperformance.
And Granny I, fell 1.2% compared to a 0.6% rise in the S&P or 65 basis points of underperformance.
Year-to-date, Granny is up 7.5% compared to an 11.7% rise in the S&P 500 or 425 basis points of underperformance.
Granny J is up 1.6% compared to 16% for the Russell 2500 or 1469 basis points of underperformance.
And Granny I is up 7% compared to an 11.77% for the S&P or 472 basis points of underperformance.
Now, you might be wondering what's behind, why Granny has been suffering recently.
And you know, I think a lot of it has to do with this blue tsunami, which investors think is bad for tech and AI, but I think ultimately it's good.
And let me explain.
Here are some of the components of the AI trade, and AI is one of the themes within Granny.
There's semiconductors, there's memory, neo clouds, and the power bottlenecks.
And these have seen a drawdown, very severe drawdown since June 30th.
The biggest of these being the neo clouds, but there's been a big drawdown in memory.
And if you look at these charts, you can see that the drawdown really steepened or declined more severely in the weeks leading up to the midterm elections.
And the midterm elections did see a blue tsunami, which the prediction markets and the polls got right.
The Democratic Party went to a pretty significant majority, 54 to 56 seats.
We'll have to see the final number.
And that's a gain of as many as nine seats in the Senate.
And that's of course why it is a blue tsunami.

You know, we may have gridlock, which markets tend to like, but we also know that because we have a Republican White House and a Democratic-controlled Congress, that if anything's going to get done, it requires compromise.
And in fact, President Trump said he's willing to work with the Democrats.
I think that's one of the positive outcomes here is that we could see Washington be forced to work with each other.
But I do want to give you why seven reasons that this Democratic sweep is actually bullish for markets and tech stocks.
The first is midterm seasonality, and something I've talked about before.
That if you look at historical patterns, when you have a Republican trifecta at the start of the year, and it's a midterm election year, markets bottom in early November, and then a rally ensues.
I think that's where we are today.
And we're following that pattern pretty closely.
On top of that, some of the headwinds for markets are fading.
In October, we did see a situation where oil was surging and yields are falling, which is not a bad situation, but we'd rather see both fall.
And then the oil began to flatten towards the middle of October, but yields were still falling, which is good.
But finally, we're getting both a fall in yields and in falling oil prices, and that's a good thing.
And this has led to a correction in the Nasdaq.
The Nasdaq 100 is down 11%.
So, that corrected pretty heavily into the election, and that's of course putting pressure on Granny Shots.
It's not that different than the 12% decline so that's seen between June 30th and August early August after the situation awareness blow up.
And markets are in similar oversold position.
Keep in mind after the August decline, the S&P 500 rallied 15%.
So, I think you got a 15% rally in the Nasdaq coming.
The tech sector is also not tied to a political party, so it's not a Republican Party sector.
Since but if you look at the last 20 years, we've listed above the different parties controlling the Senate and the House.
And under all configurations, you can see the Nasdaq 100 has been outperforming the S&P.
So, I think that that's going to apply today.
And as for AI, I think this there are some positives coming.
I think AI is likely to be reshaped by the Democratic Party, one that emphasizes safety and a slowdown on spending, which is going to keep this from becoming a bubble.
As you know, some of the frontier models warn of AI's capabilities to either wipe out jobs or even do harmful things.
And of course, it's called it's created a cry from the Democratic Party to protect humans, which is good.
And in fact, party leaders the Democratic Party leaders are urging the need to prioritize AI safety.

And in Texas, where we had a surprising sweep by the Democratic Party, while there's beliefs that this means the data center projects in that state are not going to go anywhere, I think the new governor prefers to actually
Just make sure that AI is constructed on her terms.
And so ultimately, it may be a delay in spending, but that's different from spending not taking place.
And the reason I think ultimately spending takes place is that there is a lot of money that's invested in the community from data centers and to the state.
Now, I think a lot of new bad news is priced in.
It may not feel like it completely today, but go back to 2016 when President Trump surprisingly emerged as the winning candidate and futures overnight tanked, but by the morning began to rally.
That's what we're witnessing today.
And we're coming at a time when investors are very risk-off.

And even things like credit default swaps, which measure default risk for things like Coreweave and Oracle, despite the negative headlines today, they're actually those yields are actually rally rallying on a relative basis.
They actually peaked more than a week ago.

Another reason why I think tech's going to work and the market works is that with a split between the White House and the party that controls Congress, I think it now allows the Fed to operate more independently.
And that's been a question dogging Kevin Warsh since he became Fed chair.
In fact, that's one of the reasons why he had to pursue that hike is to do a credibility hike and also to get the FOMC members to believe he was independent.
But I think there's going to be less harassment from the White House.
And looking back, bond markets were really unnerved when Kevin Warsh started to talk hawkishly.
That was at Jackson Hole and after the September hike, but since he's dialed down that rhetoric, bond market volatility and yields have fallen, which is a good thing.
And again, I think the pressure now is off Kevin Warsh to exert his independence and try to pursue credibility actions.
Democrats in general tend to spend more.
This is from Forbes, and it shows that when Democrats control Congress, per capita spending tends to go up.
This is reflected here, showing that when you went from a Republican Congress to Democrat, spending tended to jump.
Similarly, the opposite's true.
When you go from a Democratic Congress to a Republican Congress, spending tends to fall.
And finally, I think there's clues from crypto, because crypto is a leading indicator for stocks.

After the Binance exploit, which was happening last week, crypto fell more than 200 points, and then was climbing back until last night when the futures fell and crypto fell when it looked like a Democratic sweep was happening.
But, as you can see, with today's trading session in the US, Ethereum is back to 2450.
I think that's a sign we're in a bull market.
But, bottom line, I think that I would be buying this AI dip.
And I as much as these charts look very painful, and with the drawdowns, I think it's better to take a half full view and also be ready to buy that dip.
Now, as for as far as individual stocks go, I want to highlight a few.
The top five performers in Granny and Granny I were Vertiv, PWR, Eli Lilly, KLA, Ten Core, and Tesla.
The bottom five performers were stocks like Robinhood, Strategy.com, Alphabet, Intel, and ServiceNow.
On the junior side, the top five performers were Huntington Ingalls, SoFi, Pigeon, Lumentum Holdings, and Galaxy Digital.
The bottom five are things like MongoDB, HF Sinclair, Zeta Global, Form Factor, and Radian.
That's it for now.
Thanks for listening, and I'll speak to you soon.

vocab.zh: 表現落後；相對報酬較差
vocab.usage: relative underperformance 相對表現落後；years of underperformance 多年表現不佳
vocab.example: The fund's underperformance this month came from tech stocks.
vocab.example_zh: 這檔基金本月表現落後，主要是因為科技股。

vocab.usage: 65 basis points of underperformance 落後 65 個基點；cut rates by 25 basis points 降息 25 個基點
vocab.example: The stock lagged the index by 40 basis points.
vocab.example_zh: 這檔股票比指數落後 40 個基點。

vocab.usage: power bottlenecks 電力瓶頸；a bottleneck in supply 供應瓶頸
vocab.example: Power bottlenecks have slowed the growth of data centers.
vocab.example_zh: 電力瓶頸已經讓資料中心的成長變慢。

vocab.usage: a severe drawdown 嚴重回撤；see a drawdown 出現回撤
vocab.example: The sector has seen a severe drawdown since June.
vocab.example_zh: 這個產業自 6 月以來出現了嚴重回撤。

vocab.usage: the drawdown steepened 回撤變得更陡；steepen a decline 讓跌勢加劇
vocab.example: Losses steepened in the weeks before the election.
vocab.example_zh: 選前幾週，跌幅變得更陡。

vocab.zh: 僵局；府會對立難推動政策
vocab.usage: political gridlock 政治僵局；markets tend to like gridlock 市場往往喜歡僵局
vocab.example: Investors often prefer gridlock because fewer new laws get passed.
vocab.example_zh: 投資人往往比較喜歡政治僵局，因為新法規比較不容易過關。

vocab.usage: it requires compromise 必須妥協；reach a compromise 達成妥協
vocab.example: The two parties will have to reach a compromise on the budget.
vocab.example_zh: 兩黨必須在預算上達成妥協。

vocab.usage: a Democratic sweep 民主黨大勝；an election sweep 選舉橫掃
vocab.example: A sweep in Congress would change the balance of power.
vocab.example_zh: 若在國會大勝，權力平衡就會改變。

vocab.usage: bullish for markets / stocks 對市場／股票看好；a bullish outlook 看漲的展望
vocab.example: Many investors remain bullish on technology stocks.
vocab.example_zh: 許多投資人仍對科技股保持看好。

vocab.zh: 季節性；依季節出現的規律
vocab.usage: midterm seasonality 期中選舉的季節性；seasonal patterns 季節性規律
vocab.example: Traders watch midterm seasonality for clues about the next rally.
vocab.example_zh: 交易員會觀察期中選舉的季節性，尋找下一波反彈的線索。

vocab.zh: 三贏局面；（此處指同一政黨掌握白宮與參眾兩院）
vocab.usage: a Republican trifecta 共和黨掌握白宮與國會兩院；win the trifecta 拿下三贏
vocab.example: A party trifecta makes it easier to pass new laws.
vocab.example_zh: 同一政黨若掌握行政與國會兩院，要通過新法會比較容易。

vocab.usage: a rally ensues 隨之出現反彈；chaos may ensue 可能接著出現混亂
vocab.example: If prices stabilize, a rally may ensue.
vocab.example_zh: 若價格穩住，接著可能出現反彈。

vocab.usage: headwinds for markets 市場面臨的逆風；headwinds are fading 逆風正在減弱
vocab.example: Falling oil prices mean one of the headwinds is fading.
vocab.example_zh: 油價下跌，代表其中一道逆風正在減弱。

vocab.usage: a correction in the Nasdaq 那斯達克的修正；enter a correction 進入修正
vocab.example: The correction in the Nasdaq was sharper than many expected.
vocab.example_zh: 那斯達克的這波修正，比許多人預期的更急。

vocab.usage: an oversold position / market 超賣的位置／市場；look oversold 看起來超賣
vocab.example: After a sharp drop, the market looked oversold.
vocab.example_zh: 急跌之後，市場看起來已經超賣。

vocab.usage: outperforming the S&P 表現優於標普；outperform the market 跑贏大盤
vocab.example: Tech stocks have been outperforming the broader market this year.
vocab.example_zh: 科技股今年一直跑贏整體市場。

vocab.usage: bad news is priced in 利空已反映在價格中；priced in a rate cut 已把降息反映進去
vocab.example: A lot of the bad news may already be priced in.
vocab.example_zh: 許多利空或許已經反映在價格裡了。

vocab.zh: 避險的；風險偏好下降的
vocab.usage: investors are risk-off 投資人處於避險狀態；a risk-off mood 避險氣氛
vocab.example: When investors are risk-off, they often sell technology stocks first.
vocab.example_zh: 當投資人避險時，往往會先賣出科技股。

vocab.usage: operate more independently 更獨立地運作；act independently 獨立行動
vocab.example: The central bank wants to set policy independently.
vocab.example_zh: 中央銀行希望能獨立制定政策。

vocab.usage: a question dogging someone 一直困擾某人的問題；be dogged by delays 一直被延誤困擾
vocab.example: Questions about independence have dogged the new chair.
vocab.example_zh: 有關獨立性的疑問，一直困擾這位新主席。

vocab.usage: markets were unnerved 市場感到不安；unnerved by the news 被消息嚇到
vocab.example: Bond investors were unnerved by the sudden change in tone.
vocab.example_zh: 債券投資人被語氣的突然改變嚇到了。

vocab.usage: talk hawkishly 說話偏鷹派；act hawkishly 採取鷹派做法
vocab.example: The chair began to talk more hawkishly about inflation.
vocab.example_zh: 主席開始用更鷹派的口吻談論通膨。

vocab.usage: bond market volatility 債券市場波動；volatility has fallen 波動率已經下降
vocab.example: Bond market volatility has fallen in recent weeks.
vocab.example_zh: 近幾週債券市場的波動已經下降。

vocab.usage: a leading indicator for stocks 股市的領先指標；serve as a leading indicator 作為領先指標
vocab.example: Some investors treat crypto as a leading indicator for stocks.
vocab.example_zh: 有些投資人把加密貨幣當成股市的領先指標。

vocab.usage: buy the dip 逢低買進；an AI dip AI 相關股票的回檔
vocab.example: He plans to buy the dip if prices fall again.
vocab.example_zh: 如果價格再跌，他計畫逢低買進。
